Kitchen Equipment & Cooking method BHT3406 - 2026

Objectives 1 2 3 Understand/ be able to identify the function of kitchen equipment Be able to select a proper cutting method to match cooking purposes Understand/ be able to identify the cooking technique

Kitchen gadgets is all around Thousands of kitchen utensils fill hundreds of general department stores and specialty shops Generally they are all specialized versions of the basic three: KNIFE, FORK, SPOON!

Specialization = Convenience Most utensils have been invented to make life more convenient Some basic utensils make cooking fun because less time is spent actually preparing the food for cooking Even a microwave is just piece of kitchen equipment to make heating food easier!

Why learn these kitchen utensils ? Using the right tool for the job makes a carpenter's work easier. They would not be able to pound many nails per hour if they were using a saw. Our food preparation labs have specialized equipment that will make tasks easier, more efficient and produce products that are better quality than just using a knife, fork or spoon!

Here's how we will learn the utensils: - Look for three elements: - Picture of the utensil in the upper right. - Standard name for the utensil or piece of equipment in the title. - Function of how it is used in the kitchen - You should fill in these names and functions on your worksheet as we go along!
section: Here's how we will learn the utensils:

text: 1. Wooden Spoon - Stirring utensil that will NOT conduct heat as you stir! - Probably one of the oldest cooking utensils, which was easily carved from wood with a simple knife.
2. Rubber Scraper - Scrapes a bowl clean BUT could melt if used in a saucepan. - (rubber spatula)
3. Angle Spatula - A flexible tool for leveling off ingredients or frosting a cake or cookies. Use to lifting small food items.
4. Straight-edge Spatula A flexible tool for leveling off ingredients or frosting a cake.

5.Cake smoother and Cake Scraper - Cake smoother helps in smoothing the surface of the cake. The top and sides of the cake can be smoothened with the cake smoother. It usually has a flat surface. Sometimes, it might contain scraping parts for a quick, smooth finish.

6. Wire Whisk - Simplest tool for beating and stirring light mixtures - Whipping is one of the technique when the air is incorporate into the food which create a volume - Metal whisk should NOT be used in a nonstick pan. Instead used a plastic or rubber whisk.
7.Pastry Brush - an ordinary brush but helps spread the butter or semi-solid material over the food. Pastry brush may comprise silicone bristles or natural bristles.

8.Cakes Turntable Stand - It's the most fun and enjoyable experience for me to decorate cakes on stands. You can place your undecorated cake on it and turn it to apply different decorating materials, icing sheets of icing, buttercream, and many more. It's a must-have item if you want to decorate cakes like me. Sorry, I don't have pictures of my recently decorated cakes.

9.Cakes leveler - A cake leveler is cutting equipment that ensures the proper leveling of the cake. There are two types. One is a ring cutter with a knife, while the other might contain single thin or multiple small blades.
- Safety pinchers to easily and safely grab food items. 10. Tongs

text: 11. Dry Measuring Cups - Graduated cups to assure that the right amount of dry ingredients are used. Remember the standard set 1/4 cup, 1/3 cup, 1/2 cup, 1 cup

14. Pastry Blender - Tool for cutting shortening or butter into flour for flaky products like biscuits or pie crust. (cut in)
15. Potato Masher - Tool for mashing potatoes and other items.
16. Decorating Bags & Tips - Bag with assorted tips for decorating cakes, deviled eggs and other desserts. (nozzle)
17. Rolling Pin - Cylinder which eases the rolling of dough and pastries. - Can be made or wood or plastic
18. Sifter - Wire mesh and rotating bars for breaking up lumps or loosening flour.
19. Standard knife set sharpening steel fish knife cook's knife bread knife paring knife cleaver boning knife peeling knife
20. Kitchen Shears - Heavy scissors for cutting meat, dough, pizza and fresh herbs. - Can also loosen bottle lids and small jars. - Cracks nuts and some shellfish.
21. Can Opener - Bottle openers, hand-held crank openers and electric can openers all making opening sealed cans easier.
22. Pastry Wheel - Special blade used to cut dough or pie crusts into strips - Can have a straight or fluted edge.
23. Melon Baller - Round tool for cutting melons. - 'Parisienne Knife' is the traditional French term for this utensil.
24. Peeler - Thin blade to remove the outer surface of fruit and vegetables.
25. Apple corer - A device for removing the core and pips from an apple. It may also be used for similar fruits, such as pears or quince.
26. Grater - Various holes and blades which cut cheese and vegetables into thin strips or slices. microplane

27. Cutting Boards - Wood, Glass or Plastic surface for protecting counters when cutting foods. - Glass should never be used because it damages knives. - Plastic is the most sanitary because bacteria can live in wood cutting boards. - Make sure to buy color coded boards for food safety!
28. Oven Mitts and Hot Pads - Insulated fabric gloves or silicone used to protect hands when handling hot items.
29. Cooling Racks - Wire racks for cooling hot food or resting a meat.
30. Cooking tray - A flat baking sheet for baking goods. Cast Iron Aluminum Copper Stainless Steel Teflon

31. Silicone mat - Designed to create an even, nonstick surface on standard baking sheets with a heat resistant up to 250°C. - Its come in a variety of shapes, sizes, and colors. Baking paper (parchment paper)
32. Silicone Bakeware - Look for FDA-approved food grade silicone. It is able to use in the freezer, refrigerator, microwave, dishwasher, and oven safe.
33. Muffin Pans - An oblong pan with round depressions for baking muffins, cupcakes or any savory dishes.
35. Loaf Pan Deep construction allows for high rising Perfect for bread, cake, and pudding Excellent heat conduction permits low temperature baking for optimum results
36. Cake Pans - Various sized pans used for baking identified as width by length in inches - Common ones are: - 9'x 13' Oblong - 9'x 9' Square - 9' Round
37. Springform Cake Pan - Two-piece construction with removable sides for an easy release - Ideal for cheesecake, tortes, quiche, and other dishes that may be difficult to remove from a standard pan
38. Tube Pan - Pan with a hollow tube in the center allowing for the cake to rise and yet the center to bake evenly. (Angel Food Cake Pan)
39. Tart Pan - Straight, fluted sides for a crisp, presentable crust - Removable bottom permits taking out a tart without damaging its crust
40. Kitchen scale - Used to measure the weight of ingredients and other food
41. Strainer - A fine wire mesh used to drain liquids from smaller amounts of food. (chinois)
42. Double Boiler - Two pans that fit together so that food can be cooked over boiling water without burning. - Great for melting chocolate, butter or cooking custard.

43. Skillet Fry Pan - Cast iron, metal or glass pan with low sides and a handle used for broiling foods or cooking in a small amount of fat. - Use for frying, searing, sautéing, and browning, among other functions

44. Sauté Pan - It has a wide flat bottom and vertical sides that generally go up much higher than a skillet's flared sides do. - This makes it easier to cook sauces and sear and braise meat than a skillet.
45. Saucepan - A deep cooking pan with a handle and lid for boiling simmering and steaming foods. - Also to cook a small portion of soups, stews, pastas or sauces.

46. Large Pot - Thick base for a good slow simmer for cooking large dishes. - Smaller diameter and taller height of pot preserves liquids longer and forces the liquid to bubble up through the ingredients, maximizing flavor transfer Stock pot
47. Grill Pan - It creates tantalizing grill lines in your food, just like a barbecue does.
48. Kitchen Thermometers - A variety of thermometers to read the temperature of food or kitchen equipment - Very important to use when cooking meat to make sure meat is safe to eat!
49. Electric Stand Mixer - An appliance which can mix, beat and knead batters and dough. - Wire whisk for beating - Paddle for blending - Dough hook for mixing bread and heavy dough. Hand mixer
50. Hand blender - A kitchen blade grinder used to blend ingredients or purée food in the container in which they are being prepared.
51.Ramekins - Ramekins are nice to have for making individual portions of desserts, such as crème brûlée, but you don't necessarily need them in your kitchen.

52.Ovens - Ovens are the soul and life of every bakery. They are used to bake and cook pastries, cakes, pies, breads, cookies, and other baked goods. - Types: Combination ovens, convection ovens, conventional gas ovens, conventional electric ovens, toaster ovens, and microwave ovens.
53.Forcep - Decorate edible flower, small leaf and etc.
54.Blow Torch

Cooking Methods Dry-heat cooking, moist-heat cooking
Boiling - To cook food in liquid that has reached the highest temperature possible 100°C. Air bubbles continuously rise, break the surface and escape as steam.
Blanching - The food is par-cooked and then submerged immediately in an icebath to stop the cooking process.
Steaming - Food is in contact only with the steam produces from the boiling liquid. - Steaming is common method due to its fast cooking times, high heat and moist-heat cooking nature.
Simmering - The cooking liquid is a bit hotter than poaching - from 82°C to 96°C - The air bubbles rise slowly and just barely break the surface.
Sautéing - A form of cooking that uses a very hot pan and a small amount of fat to cook the food very quickly.
Stewing - Stewing is similar to braising because the ingredient is first seared and then cooked in liquid, but it uses smaller ingredients like diced meats and vegetables.

Braising - First the food is sautéed or seared, and then simmered in liquid for a long period of time until tender. - Pot roasts, stews and casseroles can be cooked in this way if they contain larger food items such as poultry legs.

Poaching - Cooking in liquid with a temperature ranging from 60°C to 82°C is called poaching. - It is typically reserved for cooking very delicate items like eggs and fish. The water should show slight movement and no bubbles.
Pan-frying - To cook on the frying pan at a medium-high heat. - Pan-frying involves much more oil than usual as it helps prevent moisture releasing from the ingredient.
Deep frying - The cooking method in which food is submerged in hot fat, which allow the product to cook faster and brown.

Roasting/ Baking - Slowly transfer the heat to an ingredients mainly using the oven which have a highly accurate temperature and ability to cook evenly for a long controlled periods. - Broiling only uses the top heating

Grilling - Grilling rely on heat being conducted through the air from an open flame. - This type of cooking produces browning reactions on the surface of the food, thus encouraging the development of complex flavors and aromas.

Searing - Searing is done with minimal amounts of fat over high heat. Searing foods gives them a brown, caramelized outside, while not cooking the interior fully. - Searing a thin piece of fish so that is has crispy skin and a delicate, tender inside.
Sous vide - The method of vacuum sealing food into plastic and then simmering the package in water to heat throughout which retains its natural flavor as possible.
Cutting techniques Essential terms
Mince - To chop finely
Batonnet - To cut into a thick stick. (6mm)
Julienne - To cut into long thin 'matchstick'(2mm)
Dice - To cut food into square pieces Brunoise - small dice
Slicing - To cut food into thin, relatively broad slices.
Chiffonade - To slice very thin, mostly used on herbs and vegetables cutting
